record.paper_title: Closed operator inequalities and open problems
record.context_brief: Closures of R*U and C*S0 inequalities
record.original_question: Let H be a complex Hilbert space and let B(H) be the C*-algebra of all bounded linear operators on H. Let I(H) be the class of invertible operators in B(H). Let C*S0(H) be the class of all invertible normal operators in B(H) whose spectra are contained in straight lines passing through the origin. Let R*U(H) be the class of all S in I(H) such that ||S X S^-1|| + ||S^-1 X S|| = 2||X|| for every X in B(H). For a relation R(S,X), call a proposition closed in B(H) x B(H) when its operator class is exactly the set of all S in B(H) for which R(S,X) holds for every X in B(H). Determine the closures of both of the following operator inequalities: first, for every S in R*U(H) and every X in B(H), ||S X S^-1 + S^-1 X S|| <= 2||X||; second, for every S in C*S0(H) union R*U(H) and every X in B(H), ||S X S^-1 + S^-1 X S|| <= ||S* X S^-1 + S^-1 X S*||, where S* denotes the adjoint of S.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $B(H)$ denote the C*-algebra of all bounded linear operators on $H$, with operator norm $\|\cdot\|$ and adjoint $X \mapsto X^*$. Let $I(H)$ be the set of invertible elements of $B(H)$. Define the following two subclasses of $I(H)$:
- $C^*S_0(H)$: the class of all invertible normal operators $S \in B(H)$ whose spectrum is contained in a union of straight lines passing through the origin of $\mathbb{C}$;
- $R^*U(H)$: the class of all $S \in I(H)$ such that $\|SXS^{-1}\| + \|S^{-1}XS\| = 2\|X\|$ for every $X \in B(H)$.

For a binary relation $R(S,X)$ on $B(H) \times B(H)$, say that the proposition "for every $X \in B(H)$, $R(S,X)$ holds" is closed in $B(H)$ if the set $\{S \in B(H) : R(S,X) \text{ holds for every } X \in B(H)\}$ equals exactly the class of operators on which this proposition is asserted to hold. The closure of an inequality "for every $S$ in a class $\mathcal{C}$ and every $X \in B(H)$, $R(S,X)$ holds" is the largest such class $\widehat{\mathcal{C}} \supseteq \mathcal{C}$ for which the statement remains true; i.e. $\widehat{\mathcal{C}} = \{S \in B(H) : R(S,X) \text{ holds for every } X \in B(H)\}$.

Determine the closures (in this sense) of each of the following two operator inequalities:

(1) For every $S \in R^*U(H)$ and every $X \in B(H)$,
$$\|SXS^{-1} + S^{-1}XS\| \le 2\|X\|.$$

(2) For every $S \in C^*S_0(H) \cup R^*U(H)$ and every $X \in B(H)$,
$$\|SXS^{-1} + S^{-1}XS\| \le \|S^*XS^{-1} + S^{-1}XS^*\|.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The two inequalities are explicitly listed as open problems in the paper "Closed operator inequalities and open problems" (Mathematical Inequalities & Applications, 14(12)), and no subsequent published resolution of the closures of these particular inequalities was found in a web search.

status_evidence.title: Closed operator inequalities and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: The paper reformulates previous characterizations of subclasses of complex Hilbert space normal operators using the concept of closed inequalities and presents some open problems concerning closed inequalities.
status_evidence.claim: The inequalities concerning R*U(H) and C*S0(H) are presented as open problems.
